patterns_data.top_pattern: VA authorized acute spend is concentrating in a few hospital systems
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: VA / ACUTE HOSPITAL / DSNP HMO, Medicare HMO, CSNP HMO / Y
patterns_data.pattern_details: VA acute hospital spend rose sharply across auth-required Medicare products, with the increase clustering in a small number of hospitals rather than being broadly spread. Most of the growth is admission-driven, but selected hospitals also show higher paid per admit. This is both a utilization issue and a provider concentration issue, especially within the Sentara, VCU, Carilion, and Chippenham footprint.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A concentrated hospital mix gives the plan a focused opportunity to address medical necessity, contract performance, and provider-specific practice patterns.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM and network review on the named hospitals by product to test admission appropriateness, length-of-stay patterns, and contract performance before broad policy changes.
evidence_summary: VA DSNP HMO acute hospital spend rose +$99.0M with 6,177 more admissions and +$1.3K paid per admit.
VA Medicare HMO acute added +$64.3M with 3,834 more admissions; Carilion and VCU each contributed about +$6.2M to +$6.6M.
VA CSNP HMO acute added +$26.3M on 1,740 more admissions, even as paid per admit fell.
Within DSNP HMO, Sentara Norfolk General and Sentara Leigh added about +$7.6M and +$5.2M.

patterns_data.top_pattern: TX authorized acute growth is mainly an admission spike
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: TX / ACUTE HOSPITAL / DSNP HMO, CSNP HMO / Y
patterns_data.pattern_details: TX acute hospital growth under auth-required Medicare products is primarily a utilization story. DSNP HMO and CSNP HMO both show materially more admissions, while payment per admit is flat to down. The business lever here is inpatient management and avoidable admission prevention, not broad reimbursement escalation.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When spend growth is volume-led, the fastest savings lever is controlling avoidable acute utilization rather than renegotiating rates.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Target TX DSNP HMO and CSNP HMO inpatient admission management, including front-end authorization review, avoidable admit analysis, and care coordination for high-admit members.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO acute added +$75.9M on 3,685 more admissions, with paid per admit essentially flat.
TX CSNP HMO acute added +$9.8M on 449 more admissions while paid per admit fell about $257.
The pattern is concentrated in auth-required acute care rather than broad facility expansion.

key_driver_codes: Amputation for Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue Disorders with CC

patterns_data.pattern_details: TX has a material authorization classification shift, and part of the same spend is also landing in an unmapped facility bucket. That means the plan should not treat all of this as true utilization or reimbursement change until the authorization field and facility mapping are reconciled. The issue is large enough to distort product and site-of-care actions.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Acting on unstable authorization or facility attribution can send UM and network teams after the wrong problem.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile TX authorization field logic and facility mapping for DSNP HMO, then rerun the market readout before changing prior auth policy or provider actions.
patterns_data.validation_reason: A large share of TX change is tied to authorization classification movement and unmapped facility attribution.
evidence_summary: TX authorization classification movement accounts for about +$53.8M of change.
TX DSNP HMO spend in Not Mapped facility type adds +$9.3M on 252 admissions with about +$21.0K paid per admit.
Named drivers within the validation signal include amputation and digestive DRGs, but the core issue is attribution stability first.

patterns_data.top_pattern: VA authorization coding movement is distorting hospital attribution
patterns_data.pattern_details: VA shows a large movement in authorization coding that is concentrated in the same hospitals driving the biggest acute spend increases. Until that coding shift is reconciled, provider comparisons and auth-related actions may be misdirected. This is a gating data-quality issue for both UM and network teams.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If hospital attribution is unstable, the plan risks taking provider action on coding movement rather than true performance change.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Audit authorization feed logic and provider submission patterns for the named hospitals, then refresh provider-level attribution before escalating contract or UM interventions.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Material spend movement is tied to authorization classification changes across several high-impact VA hospitals.
evidence_summary: VA authorization classification movement totals +$45.5M.
VCU Medical Center and Chippenham Hospital lead the shift at about +$12.2M and +$11.1M.
Carilion adds about +$9.0M, with Sentara Norfolk General and Sentara Leigh adding about +$6.3M and +$6.9M.

patterns_data.top_pattern: VA post-acute spending is shifting into SNF and NF care
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: VA / SNF - FREE STANDING and NF / DSNP HMO, Medicare HMO
key_driver_codes: Bone Diseases and Arthropathies with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: VA post-acute growth is showing up primarily in SNF and NF settings rather than only in acute hospitals. The largest piece is DSNP HMO SNF volume without authorization, with additional contribution from musculoskeletal and osteomyelitis-related NF cases and pockets of higher paid per admit. This points to a post-acute site-of-care management opportunity.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Rapid SNF and NF growth can erode savings if placement, length of stay, and preferred-facility steering are not tightly managed.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Tighten post-acute placement criteria and preferred SNF steering in VA, and run concurrent review on musculoskeletal and osteomyelitis-related SNF/NF stays.
evidence_summary: VA DSNP HMO SNF without authorization added +$50.9M on 5,828 more admissions.
Additional VA SNF mixed pressure added +$1.1M, led by Bone Diseases and Arthropathies with MCC.
VA NF musculoskeletal cases added +$771K, led by bilateral primary knee osteoarthritis at +$346K.
Rare VA NF osteomyelitis cases added +$294K on low volumes.

patterns_data.top_pattern: OH has a focused cardiac ablation cost-intensity spike
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: OH / IP Med/Surg and ACUTE HOSPITAL / Medicare HMO
key_driver_codes: Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Closure and Cardiac Ablation
patterns_data.pattern_details: OH shows a concentrated inpatient cardiac pattern rather than broad Med/Surg inflation. Cases involving concomitant left atrial appendage closure and cardiac ablation increased, and paid per admit also rose materially for atrial fibrillation diagnoses. This is a focused clinical and reimbursement issue appropriate for targeted review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A narrow, high-cost procedure cluster can often be addressed faster with targeted clinical policy and payment review than with broad utilization programs.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send this to clinical and reimbursement policy review for appropriateness criteria, episode design, and provider payment terms for these cardiac ablation cases.
evidence_summary: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation cases tied to concomitant left atrial appendage closure and cardiac ablation added +$3.2M on 59 admissions with about +$10.6K paid per admit.
Persistent atrial fibrillation added another +$2.0M on 35 admissions with about +$8.8K paid per admit.
Operational Medicare HMO acute hospital signal adds +$3.1M on 61 admissions with about +$8.0K paid per admit.

key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
Amputation for Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue Disorders with CC
OTH POSTPROC COMP D/O DIGESTIVE SYS
patterns_data.pattern_details: TX has a focused inpatient complication pattern, led by digestive and post-procedure cases, with amputation and osteomyelitis cases adding smaller but costly spikes. Part of the signal is true volume and intensity growth, and part is rare high-cost case emergence. This is best handled as a targeted clinical management issue rather than a broad network or pricing issue.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Complication-driven inpatient clusters can create avoidable high-cost episodes if not addressed through case management and clinical pathways.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route to clinical review for complication prevention, infection management, and case management on digestive complication and amputation-related admissions.
evidence_summary: TX IP Med/Surg complications added +$2.0M, led by post-procedure digestive complications at +$504K and vascular disorder of intestine at +$335K.
Additional rare osteomyelitis and amputation cases added +$235K, including one admission at about +$179K.
Several of the amputation and osteomyelitis cases are low-volume, so the right response is targeted case review rather than broad policy change.

patterns_data.top_pattern: WA shows a small but emerging authorized non-acute cost cluster
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: WA / DSNP HMO / CRITICAL ACCESS, SNF - FREE STANDING, Physical Rehab
patterns_data.pattern_details: WA is not a top-dollar market, but it is showing an emerging authorized cost cluster across critical access, SNF, and physical rehab settings. The market also has a material authorization classification movement, so the signal should be treated as early-stage and validated before scaling action. After validation, the likely business question is whether referrals are moving into higher-cost non-acute settings.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Small emerging site-of-care changes can become expensive quickly if they are validated late.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Validate WA authorization coding first, then review whether DSNP HMO referrals are shifting into higher-cost critical access, SNF, or rehab settings.
patterns_data.validation_reason: WA includes a material authorization classification shift alongside a small but growing non-acute site mix signal.
evidence_summary: WA authorization classification movement adds about +$1.3M.
WA critical access adds +$374K on 17 admissions with about +$4.8K paid per admit.
WA SNF adds +$340K on 11 admissions, and physical rehab adds +$195K on 3 admissions with about +$18.9K paid per admit.
